newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices gain, supplies hit by strike.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices gain, supplies hit by strike.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Thursday rose after supplies were affected by an ongoing strike by truckers, dealers said.

Indian truck operators have been on strike since April 1 to protest against a service tax and a hike in the insurance premium. The strike has cut sharply the movement of cotton from producing centres to millers, a dealer said.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by 10 rupees at 900/940 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned rose by 10 rupees at 1,560/1,660 rupees per maund.
Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) lifted by 200/300 rupees to 13,500/13,800 rupees per candy (355.56 kg). Some millers say there is a shortage of ready stock.
"If the transport strike is prolonged then we will have to reduce production and curtail the daily shift," a miller said.
Overall market sentiment remained firm at the close. Traders said they were expecting more buying by the spinning mills.
